The search turned up several GitHub issues where browser extensions were blamed for React 19 hydration mismatches. None of them is a confirmed React bug fix.

- **Extension-injected DOM nodes:** React's own hydration error text says an extension that alters the HTML before React loads can trigger it. It can also happen if the client has a browser extension installed which messes with the HTML before React loaded. Issue #36169 is a separate case, a `<script defer>` inside `<head>` on React 19.2.4, and it is still open.
- **Specific extensions:** In Next.js issue #31895, a Video Speed Controller extension was implicated, but the issue was Closed as not planned. In Vercel discussion #72035, the ColorZilla extension added a `cz-shortcut-listen` attribute to the page. The workaround was a small client script that removes the attribute before hydration and watches to keep it from returning. One user reported that when Colorzilla is disabled, the hydration error resolves.
- **Older reports:** Issue #25924, filed against React 18.2.0, traced intermittent errors to a script tag that the React DevTools extension injected after the body tag. Issue #24430 described a similar problem from a plugin, and it was left in backlog.
- **Unrelated 19.1 bug:** Issue #33133 covers a different problem. Using `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` together with `suppressHydrationWarning` can replace server-rendered HTML with empty content. It was also Closed as not planned.

Overall, the React team has generally treated extension-caused mismatches as third-party issues. Workarounds include disabling the extension, removing the injected attribute or node before hydration, or testing in a clean browser profile.

content.text:
Yes, there are several. The closest match is the Next.js and React 19 report below, but I only read search results, not the issue pages. The status and details come from search snippets, so check them on GitHub.

- **React 19 with a browser extension:** [facebook/react-style issue #31895](https://github.com/react/react/issues/31895) is a hydration error with the Video Speed Controller extension, on `next@15.0.4-canary.41` and React `19.0.0-rc`. The search result listed it under `react/react`, not `facebook/react`, so confirm the repo. It looks like it was closed as not planned.
- **ColorZilla:** [vercel/next.js Discussion #72035](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions/72035) covers Next.js 15 with React 19. The extension injects a `cz-shortcut-listen="true"` attribute. The workaround is to remove the attribute before hydration or disable the extension.
- **Older, React 18 but the same cause:** [facebook/react #25924](https://github.com/facebook/react/issues/25924) says scripts injected by browser extensions, such as React DevTools, can cause hydration errors. [facebook/react #24430](https://github.com/facebook/react/issues/24430) reports a plugin that generates a script tag at the top of the page.

The React team seems to treat these as caused by third-party extensions, not as React bugs. The usual advice is to test in a clean browser profile or disable the extension. A narrower option is `suppressHydrationWarning` on the affected element, such as `<html>` or `<body>`.
